lines.en: The Apprentice
Every Saturday at midnight, the old clock in the square started to run backwards.
lines.tr: Her cumartesi gece yarısı, meydandaki eski saat geriye doğru işlemeye başlıyordu.

lines.en: Nobody in Haldenberg knew why.
The clock had worked perfectly for more than a hundred years.
lines.tr: Saat yüz yılı aşkın bir süredir kusursuz çalışmıştı.

chunks.en: for more than a hundred years

lines.en: Now, once a week, its long black hands turned the wrong way, slowly, for almost an hour.
lines.tr: Şimdiyse haftada bir, uzun siyah akrebi ve yelkovanı neredeyse bir saat boyunca yavaş yavaş ters yöne dönüyordu.

lines.en: Then they stopped.
Aziz saw it for the first time from the small window of his room above the clock shop.
lines.tr: Aziz bunu ilk kez, saatçi dükkânının üstündeki odasının küçük penceresinden gördü.

lines.en: He was seventeen, and he had arrived in the mountains only two weeks before.
lines.tr: On yedi yaşındaydı ve dağlara daha iki hafta önce gelmişti.

lines.en: He had come to spend the summer with Mrs Ilse Brandt, who was seventy-one and the only clockmaker in the town.
lines.tr: Yazı, yetmiş bir yaşındaki ve kasabanın tek saatçisi olan Bayan Ilse Brandt'ın yanında geçirmeye gelmişti.

lines.en: Haldenberg was a quiet place.
There were dark green forests on every side, a cold river, a bakery, a café and a square with a tall stone tower.
lines.tr: Dört bir yanda koyu yeşil ormanlar, soğuk bir nehir, bir fırın, bir kafe ve yüksek taş kuleli bir meydan vardı.

lines.en: "Who would do something like that?"
Aziz whispered.
"And why?"
The clock did not answer.
Its hands were still moving the wrong way.
Aziz had always loved machines.
At home in the city, he used to open old radios and watches just to see how they worked.
lines.tr: Şehirdeki evinde, sırf nasıl çalıştıklarını görmek için eski radyoları ve saatleri açardı.

lines.en: Most of them never worked again.
His science teacher had noticed this, and she had written a letter to Mrs Brandt.
lines.tr: Fen öğretmeni bunu fark etmiş ve Bayan Brandt'a bir mektup yazmıştı.

lines.en: "I have a student who can't stop asking how things work," she had written.
lines.tr: "Her şeyin nasıl çalıştığını sormadan duramayan bir öğrencim var," diye yazmıştı.

lines.en: "Can you teach him?"
Mrs Brandt was small and thin, with short white hair and very small feet in green shoes.
lines.tr: Bayan Brandt ufak tefek ve zayıftı; kısa beyaz saçları vardı, yeşil ayakkabıların içindeki ayakları da çok küçüktü.

lines.en: She moved quickly around the shop, and she hummed old songs while she worked.
lines.tr: Dükkânda hızlı hızlı dolaşır, çalışırken eski şarkılar mırıldanırdı.

lines.en: The shop was full of clocks: clocks on the walls, clocks on the tables, clocks inside boxes.
lines.tr: Dükkân saatlerle doluydu: duvarlarda saatler, masalarda saatler, kutuların içinde saatler.

lines.en: All of them were ticking, and all of them showed exactly the same time.
lines.tr: Hepsi tik tak ediyordu ve hepsi tam olarak aynı saati gösteriyordu.

lines.en: At the back of the shop there was a storeroom with a small, low door that was always locked.
lines.tr: Dükkânın arkasında, her zaman kilitli duran küçük, alçak bir kapısı olan bir depo vardı.

lines.en: "Only old boxes in there," Mrs Brandt had said.
lines.tr: "Orada yalnızca eski kutular var," demişti Bayan Brandt.

lines.en: "A clock that is wrong is worse than no clock," she told Aziz on his first day.
lines.tr: "Yanlış giden bir saat, hiç saat olmamasından daha kötüdür," dedi Aziz'e ilk gününde.

lines.en: "Remember that."
On Sunday morning, Aziz went to the café in the square for breakfast.
lines.tr: Pazar sabahı Aziz kahvaltı için meydandaki kafeye gitti.

lines.en: Marta, the owner, put a cup of hot chocolate in front of him.
lines.tr: Kafenin sahibi Marta önüne bir fincan sıcak çikolata koydu.

lines.en: "Did you see it last night?" she asked.
"I saw it," said Aziz.
"It ran backwards and stopped at a quarter past nine."
lines.tr: "Geriye doğru gitti ve dokuzu çeyrek geçe durdu."

lines.en: At the next table, Mr Hofer, the baker, put down his newspaper.
lines.tr: Yan masada fırıncı Bay Hofer gazetesini bıraktı.

lines.en: "It's a ghost," he said loudly.
"My grandmother always said there was a ghost in that tower."
lines.tr: "Büyükannem o kulede bir hayalet olduğunu hep söylerdi."

lines.en: "Or it's a person," said a woman near the window.
lines.tr: "Ya da bir insan," dedi pencerenin yanındaki bir kadın.

lines.en: She was looking at Aziz.
"Only two people have a key to the tower.
Mrs Brandt, who is seventy-one.
And her new apprentice."
The café went very quiet.
Aziz felt his face turn hot.
"It started on my first weekend here," he said.
"I know.
But it isn't me."
In the corner, five old people were sitting together at a round table.
lines.tr: Köşede beş yaşlı insan yuvarlak bir masada birlikte oturuyordu.

lines.en: They didn't say anything.
One of them, a tall man with a grey beard, was smiling into his coffee.
lines.tr: İçlerinden biri, gri sakallı uzun boylu bir adam, kahvesine bakarak gülümsüyordu.

lines.en: That afternoon, Aziz asked Mrs Brandt if he could go up the tower.
lines.tr: O öğleden sonra Aziz, Bayan Brandt'a kuleye çıkıp çıkamayacağını sordu.

lines.en: "Why?" she asked, without looking up from a tiny watch.
lines.tr: "Neden?" diye sordu kadın, küçücük bir saatten başını kaldırmadan.

lines.en: "Because people think I'm the ghost," he said.
lines.tr: "Çünkü insanlar hayaletin ben olduğumu düşünüyor," dedi.

lines.en: "If I find out what's happening, they will believe me."
She was quiet for a moment.
Then she gave him the big iron key.
lines.tr: Sonra ona büyük demir anahtarı verdi.

lines.en: "My knees are too old for those stairs," she said.
lines.tr: "Dizlerim o merdivenler için fazla yaşlı," dedi.

lines.en: "I haven't been up there for years.
Be careful."
The tower was dark and cold inside.
Aziz climbed ninety-nine stone steps until he reached the room behind the face of the clock.
lines.tr: Aziz saat kadranının arkasındaki odaya varana kadar doksan dokuz taş basamak çıktı.

lines.en: It was full of metal wheels of every size.
lines.tr: Oda her boyutta metal çarklarla doluydu.

lines.en: Some were as big as a table, and some were as small as a coin.
lines.tr: Bazıları bir masa kadar büyüktü, bazıları da bir madeni para kadar küçük.

lines.en: Light came through the white glass of the clock face, and the whole room seemed to shine.
lines.tr: Saat kadranının beyaz camından ışık giriyordu ve bütün oda parlıyor gibiydi.

lines.en: He put his hand on the biggest wheel.
lines.tr: Elini en büyük çarkın üstüne koydu.

lines.en: Then he looked at his fingers.
They were shiny, and they smelled of fresh oil.
Somebody had been here, and not very long ago.
lines.tr: Biri buraya gelmişti, hem de çok uzun zaman önce değil.

lines.en: Footprints
Aziz didn't tell anyone about the oil.
He wasn't sure who he could trust.
On Monday, he went up the tower again, this time with a torch.
lines.tr: Pazartesi günü kuleye yine çıktı, bu sefer yanında bir el feneriyle.

lines.en: The stairs were covered in grey dust, because nobody ever cleaned them.
lines.tr: Merdivenler gri tozla kaplıydı, çünkü kimse onları hiç temizlemiyordu.

lines.en: In the light of the torch, he saw footprints.
Most of them were small, much smaller than his own.
lines.tr: Çoğu küçüktü, onunkilerden çok daha küçük.

lines.en: Others were bigger, but they were mixed together and hard to see.
lines.tr: Diğerleri daha büyüktü, ama birbirine karışmışlardı ve zor görünüyorlardı.

lines.en: He bent down and looked closely.
The small prints had a pattern of tiny stars on them.
lines.tr: Küçük izlerin üzerinde minik yıldızlardan bir desen vardı.

lines.en: "It might be a child," he thought.
"But why would a child climb a clock tower at midnight?"
lines.tr: "Ama bir çocuk neden gece yarısı bir saat kulesine tırmansın?"

lines.en: He took a photo of the prints with his phone and went back down.

lines.en: In the shop, Mrs Brandt was waiting for him with two cups of tea.
lines.tr: Dükkânda Bayan Brandt iki fincan çayla onu bekliyordu.

lines.en: "Well?" she asked.
"Have you caught your ghost yet?"
"Not yet," said Aziz.
"But I've found its feet."
She laughed so suddenly that some of her tea went on the table.
lines.tr: Öyle aniden güldü ki çayının bir kısmı masaya döküldü.

lines.en: On Wednesday, the café was almost empty, and Marta had time to talk.
lines.tr: Çarşamba günü kafe neredeyse boştu ve Marta'nın konuşacak vakti vardı.

lines.en: Aziz was eating apple cake while she was cleaning the coffee machine.
lines.tr: Marta kahve makinesini temizlerken Aziz elmalı kek yiyordu.

lines.en: "This square used to be the happiest place in the mountains," she said.
lines.tr: "Bu meydan eskiden dağların en mutlu yeriydi," dedi.

lines.en: "Every Saturday evening there was music here.
People came from all the villages in the valley.
They used to dance until midnight."
"What happened?" asked Aziz.
"The last bus happened," said Marta.
"The bus that came up from the valley used to arrive at a quarter past seven every Saturday, full of young people.
lines.tr: "Vadiden çıkan otobüs her cumartesi yediyi çeyrek geçe, gençlerle dolu gelirdi.

lines.en: The music always started when it arrived.
Then, thirty years ago, they stopped the bus.
lines.tr: Sonra, otuz yıl önce, otobüsü kaldırdılar.

lines.en: The young people stopped coming, and the band stopped playing.
lines.tr: Gençler gelmez oldu, bando da çalmayı bıraktı.

lines.en: That was the end of it."
She looked out at the empty square for a long time.
"Have you ever danced in a square under the stars?" she asked.
lines.tr: "Hiç yıldızların altında bir meydanda dans ettin mi?" diye sordu.

lines.en: "Never," said Aziz.
"Then you've missed something wonderful," she said.

lines.en: By the next Saturday, the story of the backwards clock had travelled all the way down the valley.

lines.en: Families had brought chairs.
Children were running around in their coats.
Mr Hofer was selling warm bread from a table and telling everyone about his grandmother's ghost.

Nobody went in, and nobody came out.
At exactly midnight, the big hands shook.

A quarter past eight.
Everyone clapped, as if it was a show.

Back in his room, Aziz couldn't sleep.
He took out a notebook and wrote down everything that he knew.

lines.tr: On ikiye çeyrek kala bir şey duydu.

lines.en: It didn't come from the tower door.
It came from below, from somewhere deep inside the stone, as if a heavy old door was opening under the stairs.
lines.tr: Aşağıdan, taşın derinliklerinde bir yerden geliyordu; sanki merdivenlerin altında ağır, eski bir kapı açılıyordu.

lines.en: Then there were footsteps.
Not one person.
Several people.
They were climbing slowly, and somebody was breathing hard.
lines.tr: Yavaş yavaş tırmanıyorlardı ve biri zorlukla nefes alıyordu.

lines.en: "Shh!" said a voice.
"I am being quiet," said another voice.
lines.tr: "Sessiz duruyorum zaten," dedi başka bir ses.

lines.en: "It's my knees that are making the noise."
Somebody laughed very softly.
lines.tr: Biri çok yumuşak bir sesle güldü.

lines.en: Aziz held his breath.
His heart was beating so loudly that he was sure they could hear it.
lines.tr: Kalbi öyle yüksek sesle çarpıyordu ki onların duyabileceğinden emindi.

lines.en: The footsteps came closer and closer.
A soft yellow light moved on the wall.
lines.tr: Duvarda yumuşak, sarı bir ışık hareket etti.

lines.en: The ghosts came into the clock room.
From behind the wheel, Aziz could only see their shadows on the wall.
lines.tr: Aziz çarkın arkasından yalnızca duvardaki gölgelerini görebiliyordu.

lines.en: They were moving carefully, as if they knew every corner of the room.
lines.tr: Odanın her köşesini biliyorlarmış gibi dikkatle hareket ediyorlardı.

lines.en: One shadow was carrying a lamp.
One was carrying something big and square on its back.
lines.tr: Bir başkası sırtında büyük, köşeli bir şey taşıyordu.

lines.en: One small shadow went straight to the centre of the machine.
lines.tr: Küçük bir gölge doğruca makinenin ortasına gitti.

lines.en: He heard the sound of metal.
A small door opened somewhere in the clock.
lines.tr: Saatin içinde bir yerde küçük bir kapak açıldı.

lines.en: Then there was a long, careful click.
lines.tr: Sonra uzun, dikkatli bir tık sesi geldi.

lines.en: The ticking stopped.
For a second, the room was completely silent.
lines.tr: Bir an için oda tamamen sessizleşti.

lines.en: Down in the square, the crowd went silent too.
Then the great wheels began to turn the other way.
lines.tr: Sonra büyük çarklar ters yöne dönmeye başladı.

lines.en: "Perfect," said the small shadow.
"Exactly on time."
Aziz knew that voice.
He had heard it every day for a month.
He had heard it humming old songs over tiny watches.
lines.tr: Küçücük saatlerin başında eski şarkılar mırıldanırken duymuştu.

lines.en: He stood up and switched on his torch.
lines.tr: Ayağa kalktı ve el fenerini yaktı.

lines.en: Six faces turned towards the light.
There was Mrs Brandt, with a small can of oil in her hand and her green shoes on her feet.
lines.tr: Karşısında elinde küçük bir yağ kutusu, ayaklarında yeşil ayakkabılarıyla Bayan Brandt vardı.

lines.en: Behind her stood the five old people from the round table in the café.
lines.tr: Arkasında kafedeki yuvarlak masanın beş yaşlısı duruyordu.

lines.en: The tall man with the grey beard had an accordion case on his back.
lines.tr: Gri sakallı uzun adamın sırtında bir akordeon çantası vardı.

lines.en: A woman in a red scarf was holding the lamp.
lines.tr: Kırmızı eşarplı bir kadın lambayı tutuyordu.

lines.en: A short man was carrying a small drum, and two others had violin cases under their arms.
lines.tr: Kısa boylu bir adam küçük bir davul taşıyordu, iki kişinin de koltuğunun altında keman çantaları vardı.

lines.en: Nobody screamed.
Nobody ran.
Mrs Brandt looked at Aziz, and then she looked at her watch.
lines.tr: Bayan Brandt Aziz'e baktı, sonra da saatine.

lines.en: "Good evening, Aziz," she said quietly.
"You're late.
We started without you."
Seven Fifteen
"You?" said Aziz.
"All of you?"
"All of us," said Mrs Brandt.
"This is Otto, Rosa, Hanne, Bernard and Klaus.
lines.tr: "Bunlar Otto, Rosa, Hanne, Bernard ve Klaus.

lines.en: Thirty years ago, we were the band and the best dancers in the valley."
lines.tr: Otuz yıl önce vadinin bandosu ve en iyi dansçıları bizdik."

lines.en: Otto, the man with the grey beard, bowed.
lines.tr: Gri sakallı adam Otto eğilerek selam verdi.

lines.en: "I'm the accordion," he said.
Mrs Brandt explained while the hands moved backwards.
lines.tr: Kollar geriye doğru dönerken Bayan Brandt anlattı.

lines.en: Her father had looked after this clock before her, and there was an old passage from her storeroom to the tower.
lines.tr: Kendisinden önce bu saate babası bakmıştı ve onun deposundan kuleye uzanan eski bir geçit vardı.

lines.en: She knew how to make the clock run the other way.
lines.tr: Saati ters yöne nasıl çalıştıracağını biliyordu.

words.make: yapmak; (make it run: çalıştırmak, make it right: düzeltmek)

lines.en: "When the bus stopped, the dances stopped," she said.
"We have asked the town for years to bring them back.
Every time, they said, 'Who will come?'
So we decided to show them."
lines.tr: Biz de onlara göstermeye karar verdik."

lines.en: "A ghost brings a crowd," said Rosa, smiling.
"A dance doesn't, until it starts."
Aziz pointed at the footprints with the stars.
"Those are yours."
"Dance shoes," said Mrs Brandt.
"I've had them for fifty years."
"But everyone thinks the ghost is me," said Aziz.
lines.tr: "Ama herkes hayaletin ben olduğumu düşünüyor," dedi Aziz.

lines.en: Mrs Brandt's face changed.
"I know.
That wasn't part of our plan, and I'm sorry.
lines.tr: Bu planımızın bir parçası değildi, özür dilerim.

lines.en: I didn't think they would blame you.
I was going to tell everyone tonight."
"Help us finish," said Otto, "and nobody will ever blame you again."
lines.tr: "Bitirmemize yardım et," dedi Otto, "bir daha kimse seni suçlamaz."

chunks.en: nobody will ever blame you again

words.ever: hiç (soruda); şimdiye kadar (than ever before: hiç olmadığı kadar)

lines.en: They all looked at the clock.
The hands were moving past nine, past eight.
Below, the square was so full that people were standing on the café chairs.
lines.tr: Aşağıda meydan öyle doluydu ki insanlar kafenin sandalyelerinin üstünde ayakta duruyordu.

lines.en: "Every week we turned it back one more hour," said Hanne.
lines.tr: "Her hafta onu bir saat daha geri aldık," dedi Hanne.

lines.en: "Like a countdown.
Tonight is thirty years since the last dance.
lines.tr: Bu gece son dansın üzerinden tam otuz yıl geçiyor.

lines.en: Tonight it stops at a quarter past seven, when the music used to start."
lines.tr: Bu gece, müziğin başladığı saatte, yediyi çeyrek geçe duruyor."

lines.en: Aziz looked at the great wheels.
He had studied this machine all summer.
He knew which wheel stopped the hands.
"Then let me do the last part," he said.
lines.tr: "O zaman son kısmı ben yapayım," dedi.

lines.en: He put his hand on the lever.
When the long hand reached the three, he pulled it slowly.
lines.tr: Uzun kol üçe geldiğinde kolu yavaşça çekti.

lines.en: The clock stopped at exactly a quarter past seven.
lines.tr: Saat tam yediyi çeyrek geçe durdu.

lines.en: They came down through the passage, out through the shop and into the square.
lines.tr: Geçitten indiler, dükkândan geçtiler ve meydana çıktılar.

lines.en: The crowd turned.
Hundreds of faces looked at the six old people and the young apprentice.
lines.tr: Yüzlerce yüz altı yaşlıya ve genç çırağa baktı.

lines.en: Mr Hofer's mouth fell open.

words.fell: düştü (fall → fell; fell open: açık kaldı)

lines.en: Mrs Brandt stepped forward.
She wasn't loud, but in the silence everyone could hear her.
lines.tr: Sesi yüksek değildi, ama sessizlikte herkes onu duyabiliyordu.

lines.en: "The ghost of Haldenberg has a message," she said.
"The clock says a quarter past seven, and the dance starts now."
lines.tr: "Saat yediyi çeyrek geçiyor ve dans şimdi başlıyor."

lines.en: Otto opened his accordion and began to play.
lines.tr: Otto akordeonunu açtı ve çalmaya başladı.

lines.en: Klaus hit the drum.
Rosa and Bernard took out their violins.
The music was old and fast and happy, and for a moment nobody moved.
lines.tr: Müzik eski, hızlı ve neşeliydi; bir an kimse kıpırdamadı.

lines.en: Then Marta laughed, took Mr Hofer by the hand and pulled him into the middle of the square.
lines.tr: Sonra Marta güldü, Bay Hofer'i elinden tuttu ve onu meydanın ortasına çekti.

chunks.en: took Mr Hofer by the hand

lines.en: Children followed.
Parents followed the children.
lines.tr: Anne babalar da çocukların peşinden geldi.

lines.en: Soon the whole square was turning and spinning under the stars.
lines.tr: Çok geçmeden bütün meydan yıldızların altında dönüyor, fırıl fırıl dönüyordu.

lines.en: Mrs Brandt held out her hand to Aziz.
Her feet in their star shoes hardly touched the ground.
lines.tr: Yıldızlı ayakkabılarının içindeki ayakları yere neredeyse hiç değmiyordu.

lines.en: "Now you've danced under the stars," she said.
lines.tr: "İşte artık yıldızların altında dans ettin," dedi.

lines.en: On Monday morning, Mrs Brandt gave Aziz the big iron key.
lines.tr: Pazartesi sabahı Bayan Brandt büyük demir anahtarı Aziz'e verdi.

lines.en: "A clock that is wrong is worse than no clock," she said.
lines.tr: "Yanlış giden bir saat, hiç saat olmamasından daha kötüdür," dedi.

lines.en: "Go and make it right."

words.make: yapmak; (make it run: çalıştırmak, make it right: düzeltmek)

lines.en: So Aziz climbed the ninety-nine steps once more.
lines.tr: Aziz de doksan dokuz basamağı bir kez daha çıktı.

lines.en: He oiled the wheels, checked every part and set the hands to the correct time.
lines.tr: Çarkları yağladı, her parçayı kontrol etti ve kolları doğru saate ayarladı.

lines.en: When he came down, the clock in the square was running forwards again, strong and steady.
lines.tr: Aşağı indiğinde meydandaki saat yine ileriye doğru, güçlü ve düzenli işliyordu.

lines.en: Nobody called him a ghost again.
lines.tr: Ona bir daha kimse hayalet demedi.

lines.en: The town council met that week and made a decision.
lines.tr: Kasaba meclisi o hafta toplandı ve bir karar verdi.

lines.en: The dance would return every Saturday evening, all year, and a bus would come up from the valley again.
lines.tr: Dans bütün yıl boyunca her cumartesi akşamı geri dönecek, vadiden yine bir otobüs çıkacaktı.

lines.en: On his last evening in Haldenberg, Aziz stood by the tower and watched the bus arrive.
lines.tr: Haldenberg'deki son akşamında Aziz kulenin yanında durdu ve otobüsün gelişini izledi.

lines.en: Young people got off, laughing.
The band was already waiting on the steps.
He looked up at the clock.
It said a quarter past seven, and this time it was exactly right.
lines.tr: Saat yediyi çeyrek geçiyordu ve bu sefer tam doğruydu.

lines.en: He had come to the mountains to learn how clocks worked.
lines.tr: Dağlara saatlerin nasıl çalıştığını öğrenmeye gelmişti.

lines.en: Now he was going home, and he had learned something better: what they were for.
lines.tr: Şimdi eve dönüyordu ve daha iyi bir şey öğrenmişti: saatlerin ne işe yaradığını.
